text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Intensive talks lasting a few weeks is enough to pave the way for a solution. Sir David Hannay starts his contacts in Cyprus.
- The Cyprus Stock Exchange suspends trading in Vassiliko Cement and Cyprus Cement Company
- Direct talks before June? U.N. envoy Gustave Feissel makes a good start in the new round of proximity talks.
- The owner of a dog that killed a five-year-old boy last Saturday could face a two-year jail term.
- Offshore companies blast the central bank over rules which hamper their smooth operation.
- Italians up the stakes in the battle for the control of shares in Vassiliko cement.
- Proximity talks are to quicken in pace. Their aim is duscussion at direct negotiations of the framework of a comprehensive solution to the Cyprus problem and a new constitution.
- The United Nations warns the two sides in Cyprus that if their latest initiative fails the negative impacts will be more serious now than the failure of any other initiative before.
- Two officers in the National Guard are considered suspect for collaborating with three Turks in custody on suspicion of espionage.
- Three Turks in custody on suspicion of spying had top secret documents on defence and the security of the state in their possession.
- Fifteen Iraqis in custody pending their deportation set fire to their jail cell beds.
